title: Recording: Listen, The Snow Is Falling by Yoko Ono | 1971
content:
Record Plant, New York City
Producers: John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Phil Spector
Engineers: Roy Cicala, Jack Douglas

John Lennon and Yoko Ono recorded Ono’s song ‘Listen, The Snow Is Falling’ on 29 October 1971.

The song, credited to Yoko Ono and the Plastic Ono Band, was released as the b-side of the ‘Happy Xmas (War Is Over)’ single.

Ono had written the song in November 1968, under the title ‘Snow Is Falling All The Time’. An early version appeared as part of her ‘Song For John’ medley, recorded that month.

The 1971 recording featured Ono on vocals, Lennon and Hugh McCracken on guitar, Klaus Voormann on bass guitar, Nicky Hopkins on organ and chimes, and Jim Keltner on drums and sleigh bells.

The session did not go smoothly, as the musicians initially played the song at a faster tempo, to which Ono objected. She also took umbrage at guitar and bass riffs developed by McCracken and Voormann, and wanted Hopkins to play less forcefully, telling him he was “banging” on the keyboard.

Once the song was recorded to her satisfaction, sound effects from the Record Plant library – ‘Feet In The Snow’ and ‘Strong Wind’ – were added to give it a suitably wintry feel.
